audit.whatIsWrong: Both level charts read Vladimir/Vladimir/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill against a packet levelChart of Skill/Mordekaiser/Mordekaiser/Skill/Mordekaiser/Skill/Vladimir. The content whys[] beside them already describe the packet shape exactly — whys[0] says 'farm even', whys[3] says 'this evens out', whys[5] says 'coinflip', whys[6] says 'He out-scales hard' — so the chart contradicts its own captions on five of seven rows, including saying Mordekaiser wins the 2+ item row that the caption gives to Vladimir.
audit.why: 49.51% over 677 games with a scaling drain mage: Mordekaiser owns 2-3 and 6, the lane evens where Vladimir has poke or a saved Pool, and Vladimir takes the late game.
audit.corrected: Both layers set to Skill / Mordekaiser / Mordekaiser / Skill / Mordekaiser / Skill / Vladimir as one atomic paired group, with ratings and the two contradicting phases[N].why lines rewritten.

audit.why: All four spikes[] exist and are correctly timed: Mordekaiser's level 2-3 Q+W window (Vladimir levels Sanguine Pool late so he has no escape yet), Realm of Death at 6, the first-item coinflip, and Vladimir's 2+ item takeover. Only the reasoning inside spikes[3] was wrong, not the timing.
audit.corrected: spikes[3].text rewritten for accuracy; timings untouched.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two problems. (a) The single biggest interaction in this matchup is nowhere on the page: Riot's own text for Tides of Blood (E) says it 'can be blocked by enemy units' — standing behind your own minion wave turns off Vladimir's entire poke pattern. Not one line mentions it. (b) The page invents a mechanic that does not exist: whys[6], spikes[3].text and late all say his 'percent-HP E drain' ignores max-HP stacking. Tides of Blood neither drains nor heals — Riot's text says he PAYS his own health to charge it, and it only deals damage. The drain is Transfusion (Q). There is no percent-health scaling in either description.
audit.why: Point 4 is the most important point and the minion-block is the concrete, free counterplay that decides the poke war. Meanwhile a fabricated percent-health drain would push the player into the wrong build and the wrong fight.
audit.corrected: Added the minion-block to tldr, report[0].t and report[5].t. Replaced every 'percent-HP E drain' claim with what the kit actually supports: Transfusion healing off every trade at a 4.6s rank-5 cooldown, and Tides of Blood as flat 600-range poke. Also added Sanguine Pool's real numbers — 28s at rank 1 falling to 16s, 2s untargetable — which no line carried.

enemyKit E text (no heal, no percent health)

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d both name Sanguine Pool as the matchup-defining cooldown but give no seconds at all — 'Dodges your damage. Bait it.'
audit.why: Sanguine Pool is 28s at rank 1 and still 16s maxed. That is the longest punish window either champion has and it is the entire reason the level 2-3 and level 6 all-ins work.
audit.corrected: Both entries now carry 28s at rank 1 / 16s at rank 5 and the 2-second untargetable duration.

audit.why: Mercury's Treads and MR are correct here (unlike an ADC matchup) and anti-heal is correctly prioritised — Transfusion and Hemoplague both heal, so Grievous Wounds has two targets in one kit. dontsFull[1] was headed 'Stack pure HP' with unrelated filler underneath; I gave it matching text rather than changing the itemisation advice.

edits.before: Be honest with yourself: this is where Vlad takes over. Once he hits Rylai's plus two items his percent-HP E drain ignores your max-HP stacking, Sanguine Pool dodges your R and your E-pull, and he kites your slow delayed Q from range while Q-healing through your Darkness Rise. Your bruiser-mage damage plateaus while he becomes an unkillable AP threat, so build MR and an anti-heal component, win the early-to-six windows hard, and let your team peel him in fights you can no longer solo.
